trust_center.repositoryDescription: Ultra's FedRAMP-compatible trust center — certification status, public information, public service list, Secure Configuration Guide, Ongoing Certification Report, and availability/status page. FedRAMP 20x documents are listed in the FedRAMP 20x section of the resources panel on the left side of the trust center and are viewable without a request; controlled documents are available via the document-request control.

secure_configuration_guidance.repositoryDescription: Ultra's public Secure Configuration Guide — recommended secure defaults and administrative-account guidance for customers, including a machine-readable baseline and a settings-comparison capability.

certified_services.serviceDescription: The FedRAMP-assessed cloud service offering: the Ultra Hub control plane (org/team/workspace management, identities, governance, guardrails, and telemetry) and its AWS-hosted data stores. This is the Minimum Assessment Scope, categorized Low (FedRAMP 20x Class B baseline). The product also includes a customer-deployed enforcement point that runs client-side in the customer's environment; per FedRAMP guidance a customer-deployed/hosted component is always outside the assessment scope and is not part of this certified service (where an agency deploys it, it is covered under that agency's ATO).

nonCertified.name: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
nonCertified.useCase: Underlying IaaS — compute (ECS/Fargate), database (Aurora), load balancing, KMS, and CloudTrail logging; primary region us-east-1 (also us-west-2, eu-west-1). Mitigations: least-privilege security groups, KMS encryption at rest, TLS in transit, CloudTrail logging.

nonCertified.name: Google Workspace
nonCertified.useCase: Corporate email and productivity (FedRAMP High authorized); limited handling of federal customer communications.

current.service_desc: Ultra is an agentic security platform that secures AI agents and their tool use at runtime. A customer-deployed enforcement point sits inline — authenticating, proxying, and governing every agent and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool call — while Ultra Hub delivers centralized identity, policy, guardrails, and observability across the agent runtime. Together they give organizations autonomous-runtime security: real-time visibility and control over what AI agents can access and do, so agentic AI can be deployed and scaled safely.
